name: [TFS99] 1369
description: A Cepheid in the galaxy M96 that pulsates every 30.1 days.

radius.source: Groenewegen (2020), A&A 635, A33, period relations for Galactic fundamental-mode Cepheids applied to this star's period, 30.06 d in Tanvir et al. (1999), MNRAS 310, 175, table 3 (ID 1369: log(P) 1.478); not a measurement of this star: eq. 2, log R = 0.721 log P + 1.083; the uncertainty is the relation's scatter, 0.067 dex

temperature.source: Groenewegen (2020), A&A 635, A33, period relations for Galactic fundamental-mode Cepheids applied to this star's period, 30.06 d in Tanvir et al. (1999), MNRAS 310, 175, table 3 (ID 1369: log(P) 1.478); not a measurement of this star: the luminosity of eq. 1 (M_bol = -2.95 log P - 0.98, with the nominal solar M_bol 4.74) over the radius of eq. 2, through L = 4 pi R^2 sigma T^4 with the nominal solar 5772 K (IAU 2015 Resolutions B2 (Mamajek et al. 2015, arXiv:1510.06262) and B3 (Prsa et al. 2016, arXiv:1605.09788)); the uncertainty is the 317 K by which the two relations miss the paper's own Cepheid temperatures

gravityRange.source: Luck (2018), AJ 156, 171, table 3 (the spectroscopic gravities of its Cepheid spectra)

radialVelocity.source: SIMBAD's radial velocity of M96, the Cepheid's galaxy, from 2022ApJS..261...21Y; the star's own motion within the galaxy is not measured

distance.source: Placed in M96 as the app draws it, where the star's sight line crosses the disc's midplane: 10,456,180 pc (src/objects/m96-layers/source/recipe.json: centre 10,452,014 pc, inclination 51.07 deg, line of nodes 4.57 deg). The galaxy's distance, which places the galaxy and not a star within it: Tully et al. (2023), Cosmicflows-4, ApJ 944, 94; CDS J/ApJ/944/94, table 2 (distances of individual galaxies), PGC 32192: distance modulus 30.096 ± 0.044 mag (https://cdsarc.cds.unistra.fr/viz-bin/cat/J/ApJ/944/94)

position.credit: Tanvir et al. (1999), MNRAS 310, 175, table 3 (ID 1369: 10:46:42.12 +11:52:07.0); SIMBAD holds that position, from 1999MNRAS.310..175T

text.card: A Cepheid in the galaxy M96, 10.5 million parsecs away, that swells and shrinks every 30.1 days.
text.introduction: Tanvir et al. (1999) list the logarithm of its period as 1.478: 30.1 days. It is one of the seven Cepheids their distance to the galaxy rests on.
text.locator: table 3, ID 1369: log(P), and the caption

notes: The star pulsates; it is drawn at its mean radius
Its radius and temperature are what Groenewegen (2020), A&A 635, A33's relations for Galactic Cepheids give at its period; no measurement of this star's size or temperature exists
Its radial velocity is its galaxy's; its own motion within M96 is not measured
